title: IPO-bound Razorpay partners with OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT
key_facts: Razorpay has partnered with OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT through its growth marketing platform Razorpay Engage.
Engage will help businesses prepare product catalogues and feeds, launch campaigns and track results of ChatGPT Ads.
Early participants include Fastrack, Traya, Tata Neu, Rivaah by Tanishq, Shaadi.com, Axis Max Life, Tanishq, Palmonas and NMIMS, according to Razorpay.
An AI agent built on ChatGPT Ads best practices will create and manage campaigns, with Engage's team providing human oversight.
OpenAI's Nitin Bawankule (head of enterprise sales, India) and Razorpay COO Rahul Kothari are quoted.
The deal comes as OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads in India.
quote_evidence: Under the partnership, Razorpay Engage will help businesses prepare product catalogues, structure product feeds, launch campaigns and track the performance of their ChatGPT Ads campaigns.
Razorpay COO Rahul Kothari said the partnership will allow businesses to test ChatGPT Ads without having to build the required expertise from scratch.
why_it_matters_hint: OpenAI is building an ad business in India through a local partner, so brands can buy ads inside ChatGPT answers.
notes: Economic Times page (pool item) gave no readable text; Entrackr read instead. The pool title calls Razorpay IPO-bound; that is not in the Entrackr text.
